name: acceptance-narrowed-to-jgrapht
body:
source: human directive (reported by the coordinator) — the acceptance for scanner-optimisation is narrowed to the single reference workload ~/jgrapht; the netbeans smoke test is dropped, and the netbeans-based acceptance scenarios are re-scoped onto jgrapht. This is a product decision, not re-litigated here.

inconsistency: requirements.requirement.incremental-acceptance-targets validated the design against TWO reference workloads and stated scenarios 2 and 3 with netbeans-scaled bounds ("1–5 file localized edit on netbeans re-scans in single-digit minutes", netbeans-wide signature change, "~1h+ full scan"); requirements.note.baseline-and-acceptance restated those bounds, and requirements.requirement.incremental-graph / requirements.requirement.db-splice-from-previous / domain.note.cache-store-and-splice tied measurement (and, for the domain note, the required decision measurement) to netbeans. With netbeans no longer an acceptance workload, those bounds are unmeasurable on the single candidate workload (~16s full scan) and the "two reference workloads" framing is false.

resolution [with user]: rewrote requirements.requirement.incremental-acceptance-targets to a single validated workload, jgrapht, keeping the recorded jgrapht baseline (~16s wall / 12s logged; Java frontend ~9s, ~70%; graph assembly ~1s; DB load ~2s; startup/overhead 3–4s; 21,334 nodes; 153k edges; 18 MB DB) and restating all three scenarios on jgrapht: (1) a fresh worktree is near-instant; (2) a 1–5 file localized edit re-scans materially below the recorded jgrapht full-scan baseline — the bound is a stated TARGET, not a measurement, expressed as at most half the recorded ~16s wall (~8s), with the frontend phase materially below the recorded ~9s Java-frontend baseline AND driven by the reduced target set rather than a full frontend pass over all packages (the partial-skip observable); (3) a signature change to a widely-depended-on symbol may approach a full scan but must be exact — the incremental graph equals a from-scratch full scan of the same changed tree. The AC is now measurable on jgrapht via the per-phase timing report; no netbeans-scaled bound survives.

Correction (spec review, feedback-119/120/121): the scenario-(2) clause originally also offered "or reported as `frontend-skipped` on full cache reuse". That disjunct was UNREACHABLE and is removed from all three nodes. `frontend-skipped` is set in exactly one place — the whole-tree Win-A freshness fast path gated on `git::is_fresh` (src/main.rs:1454-1465; src/timing.rs:104-108, "the whole-tree freshness fast-path ran no frontend") — and the phase-04 test asserts the marker is CLEARED after a content edit (src/main.rs:5012-5019). A 1–5 file localized content edit is by definition not the whole-tree-unchanged case, so the fast path cannot fire; leaving the disjunct would have let a no-op scan "satisfy" the localized-edit AC and conflated scenario (1). Scenario (2)'s frontend clause now names the observable the code does expose — the per-language target-set / partial-skip verdict (`should_spawn_language`, src/main.rs:667; `ReusePlan.skipped_langs`, src/incremental.rs:169-173) — while the `frontend-skipped` marker stays the whole-tree fast path's, specified by requirements.requirement.per-phase-timing-report.

Consistency sweep (same directive): requirements.stakeholder.large-repo-team (netbeans relabelled as the motivating case only, explicitly not an acceptance workload); requirements.note.baseline-and-acceptance (acceptance line moved to jgrapht; netbeans marked motivation-only); requirements.requirement.incremental-graph and requirements.requirement.db-splice-from-previous (netbeans relabelled motivation-only, AC text unchanged — both ACs are already workload-agnostic); domain.note.cache-store-and-splice (the required measurement moved from netbeans to the jgrapht reference workload).

Left unchanged, deliberately: the transient scanner-optimisation/feedback-* nodes (reviewer-owned) and every plan/Task node (the plan re-scope is the plan-writer's, rebasing on this wording). requirements.requirement.exact-ongoing-equivalence's "a signature change to a widely-depended-on symbol may legitimately approach a full scan" was left as-is — it carries no netbeans units and remains true.
